Special Oral Selection
Outline
In the entrance examination, the "Special Oral Selection" will be implemented for exceptionally outstanding applicants who wish to enroll in the Master's Program in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the Graduate School of Engineering, The University of Tokyo.
Eligible Applicants
Highly outstanding individuals who aspire to enroll in the Master's program and have the Department of Mechanical Engineering, Graduate School of Engineering, The University of Tokyo as their first choice.
Selection Method
Applicants who opt for the Special Oral Selection will be evaluated through a document review (Document screening) and an online special oral examination conducted in July. Those who pass this selection will be assigned a prospective academic advisor and will be exempted from the written examination.
Documents to be Submitted by Applicants for Selection through the Special Oral Selection
Applicants must submit the following documents (1 to 4) to the Department of Mechanical Engineering when applying to the Graduate School of Engineering between late May and early June.
1. Transcripts
Applicants must submit transcripts showing grades from their first to third year of university.
Students currently enrolled in one of the two mechanical engineering departments of The University of Tokyo (Department of Mechanical Engineering and Department of Mechano-Informatics) are exempt from this requirement.
2. A document that lists the number of credits earned up to the fourth year of university (may be omitted if included in the transcript).
3. Official English Proficiency Score (TOEFL-iBT or TOEFL-iBT Home Edition)
Applicants must submit an official TOEFL-iBT or TOEFL-iBT Home Edition score. Submission details will be announced on the Graduate School of Engineering website once finalized.
4. Special Oral Selection Forms (Form A, B, and C) for the Department of Mechanical Engineering
Applicants must submit the following forms in the prescribed format:
a) Special Oral Selection Form A
b) Special Oral Selection Form B (Inquiry sheet)
Applicants must list up to 10 preferred academic advisors and one research topic they wish to pursue in graduate school. If selected, their assigned advisor will be one of those listed.
c) Special Oral Selection Form C （A4 landscape format, a maximum of 4 pages, including the cover page, created using PowerPoint or similar software in the prescribed format）
・Research plan for the master's program (1 page, including figures/tables)
・Progress and plan of undergraduate thesis or equivalent research (1 page, including figures/tables)
・Academic background and self-assessment of undergraduate studies (1 page, including figures/tables)
Other Important Notes
・There is no disadvantage if your undergraduate research topic differs from your desired graduate research topic.
・The results of the Special Oral Selection will be promptly notified after the document review and interview selection are completed. Successful applicants will also be informed of their prospective academic advisor.
・Applicants who are not selected through the Special Oral Selection must take the written examination scheduled for late August to early September.
・All applicants must attend the in-person interview during the graduate school entrance examination period in late August to early September. Failure to attend will result in disqualification, even for those who passed the Special Oral Selection and were exempted from the written examination.
Schedule
Late May to Early June: Application period
Late June: Notification of document screening results and details regarding the Special Oral Examination schedule
July: Special Oral Examination (conducted online)
Late July: Announcement of applicants exempted from the written examination on the Mechanical Engineering website

Q&A
Q) What happened to the Integrated Master's and Doctoral Program, which was included in the application guidelines until the year before last?
A) Since the introduction of the Special Oral Examination (Master's) from last year's entrance exam, the Integrated Master's and Doctoral Program has been discontinued.
Q) If an applicant is not selected through the Special Oral Selection, does that mean it is impossible to join a laboratory with a high concentration of applicants for this selection system, no matter how good their written exam scores are?
A) We cannot provide details regarding laboratory assignments as they are directly related to the examination process. However, in general, the Department of Mechanical Engineering considers it desirable that the faculty members who can be selected under Form B of the Special Oral Selection are the same as those who can be selected by applicants taking the written examination in August.
Q) The duration of the specialized subject (Mechanical Engineering) exam has been shortened since the year before last. How will the scoring be adjusted?
A) The scoring details are directly related to the examination process and cannot be disclosed.

Intent of the questions (Mechanical Engineering subjects)
The mission of the Department of Mechanical Engineering is to promote research and education in a wide range of fields, from the so-called “four dynamics” (mechanical dynamics, material mechanics, fluid mechanics, and thermodynamics), which are the fundamentals of mechanical engineering, to its applications in the fields of environment and energy, biotechnology and medicine, design and production systems. The specialized subject examination is intended to assess the fundamental qualifications required to become a researcher or engineer who can contribute to the advancement of science and technology and to the sustainable development of human society in the broad field of mechanical engineering. The examination covers all areas of mechanical engineering, including thermal engineering, fluid engineering, mechanics of materials, dynamics and control, and machine design and manufacturing engineering.
